meta.title: Three Fact Boxes from the Nature Park

paragraphs: Three Fact Boxes from the Nature Park, posted by Mia. On Saturday, the Explorers walked in the park with Ranger Mark. He showed us three notice boards, and I copied the facts into three boxes. Read the boxes, and look for the numbers. I wrote every number in a different color. Which box is about a bird?

Box One: The Kingfisher. A kingfisher is a small bird with a bright blue back and an orange front. It sits on a branch above the river and looks at the water. Then it makes a dive and catches a small fish in its beak. The dive takes less than a second. Both parents feed the babies with small fish. The kingfisher makes its nest in a hole in the river bank. The hole is about one meter long. The life of a kingfisher is short, and most birds live for only two or three years.

Box Two: The Climbing Wall. The park has a climbing wall for beginners. The wall is six meters high, and it is open on Saturday and Sunday from nine o'clock to four o'clock. A child must be eight years old or older. Every beginner wears a helmet, and a rope keeps each climber safe. A guide stays on the ground. The guide checks every rope before the climb starts. A tired climber can walk down the stairs on the left side of the wall. One hour of climbing costs one hundred baht.

Box Three: Huts for the Night. The park has simple accommodation for families and groups. There are six wooden huts near the river. Each hut has four beds and a fan, but it has no kitchen. The huts are quiet, and at night you can hear frogs and birds. A hut costs four hundred baht for one night. You can arrive after two o'clock, and you must leave before eleven o'clock. On a busy weekend, a hut may not be available, so ask Ranger Mark early.

My Favorite Box. Leo likes the climbing wall because it is so high. I like the kingfisher because its dive is very fast. I want to take a photo of it next time. Lily thinks the huts are the best because she wants to hear the wildlife at night. Ranger Mark says that the park is open from Tuesday to Sunday, so you can see all three boxes. Which box do you like? Tell us in a message!

The second board has a drawing of a wall with the title "The Climbing Wall". The third board has a drawing of a wooden hut with the title "Huts for the Night". A man of about forty with short black hair under a green cap, a khaki shirt with two chest pockets, green trousers, and brown boots points at the first board. Nobody wears a school uniform.

On the left side of the wall are gray stairs. Bright morning light. Nobody wears a school uniform.
